title: Integrate KMS/HSM + Automated Key Rotation Evidence Reporting for Private & Dedicated
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide production-ready integrations for customer-managed keys (CMK) across AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and Cloud HSM / on-prem HSMs, plus automated cryptographic evidence/reporting for key creation, rotation, compromise checks, and usage auditing. Scope includes: (1) BYOK onboarding flows for Private & Dedicated, (2) envelope encryption wiring across object stores / DBs / KV cache, (3) orchestrated key rotation with zero-downtime rewraps, and (4) an evidence export pipeline (signed rotation manifests, access logs, and attestations) surfaced in the Console and available via API. This ticket contains design decisions, trade-offs, implementation plan, and acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Support customer-supplied CMKs for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and importable keys for on-prem HSMs
Rotation orchestrator can rotate an active CMK and atomically rewrap short-lived DEKs; no request-level downtime exceeding 500ms p50 during rotation for 99% of traffic
Automated evidence artifacts produced per rotation: signed manifest (key id, previous key id, rotation timestamp, operator id), access log snapshot for last 30d, and KMS audit event bundle
Evidence artifacts are immutable, cryptographically verifiable, and downloadable from Console and via /audit/evidence API
RBAC: only allowed roles (customer-admin + enterprise-svc) can initiate rotation or retrieve unredacted evidence; all retrievals recorded
Integration tests exercising BYOK provisioning, rotation, and evidence export exist and run in CI with simulated KMS endpoints
Security review completed and SOC/GC/Legal sign-off attached to release notes
design_notes: We will use an envelope encryption model: generate short-lived Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) on the infra stack, encrypt DEKs with customer CMKs (KMS Encrypt API) and store encrypted DEKs alongside artifacts. For cloud KMS providers use native APIs and crypto signing features (e.g., generate-data-key, asymmetric-sign for manifests). For on-prem HSMs support PKCS#11 and importable wrapped keys; provide a minimal shim running in Private control plane to mediate HSM calls. Rotation strategy: staged rotation with model versions and rolling rewrap worker pool. Evidence model: every rotation produces a signed JSON-LD manifest, persisted to WORM storage (immutable bucket) with an accompanying chain-of-custody log. Avoid storing plaintext keys. Key caching: short-lived session tokens with strict TTLs; do not cache raw CMKs. Trade-offs: full re-encryption of all data is expensive; we will rewrap DEKs only and lazily re-encrypt blobs on first write after rotation to reduce burst IO. This means evidence must record whether data was lazily rewrapped and which objects remain under previous DEKs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): Provider adapters for AWS/GCP/Azure KMS + simple HSM PKCS#11 shim; BYOK onboarding UI and CLI; KMS credential validation flows. Phase 2 (2 sprints): Rotation orchestrator service, rewrap worker implementation, DEK lifecycle management, CI integration with simulated KMS (localstack + gcp emulator). Phase 3 (1 sprint): Evidence pipeline: manifest signer (customer-supplied signer where supported), WORM persistence, Console UI + /audit/evidence API, RBAC checks and audit recording. Phase 4 (1 sprint): Load-testing/chaos (simulate KMS throttling), perf tuning, runbook & playbook creation. Rollout: start with Private beta customers, then Dedicated customers, then hosted support (hosted will default to Redwood-managed keys unless customer opts into CMK).
risk_and_mitigation: Risks: KMS provider rate limits causing rotation failures -> mitigation: built-in exponential backoff, multi-region fallback, and transparent retry with operator alerting. Risk: accidental plaintext key material exposure during HSM integration -> mitigation: memory-safe handling, no logging of raw key bytes, in-review of all paths that touch key material, mandatory security review and HSM vendor compatibility checklist. Risk: evidence chain manipulation -> mitigation: sign manifests with an asymmetric key and publish verification keys in an append-only registry; store manifests in WORM/immutable storage and periodically notarize with a ledger hash published to customer audit channel.
testing_plan: Unit tests for provider adapters; integration tests that run against local emulators to validate generate-data-key / encrypt / decrypt loops; CI job simulating rotation at scale (10k DEKs) to validate throughput and rewrap pause safety; e2e tests that assert evidence manifests exist and signatures verify; chaos tests to verify failure modes (provider outage, partial rotation) and rollback behavior. Include pen-test of HSM shim and threat modeling review.
rollout_and_validation: Start with opt-in Private customers (can enable BYOK via onboarding flow). Run canary rotation on a single tenant with <1% traffic, validate latency and error rates, and inspect signed manifests and access logs. Gradually increase to 10% then 100%. Monitor metrics: rotation_success_rate, avg_rewrap_latency, api_error_rate_during_rotation, evidence_generation_latency. Create dashboard and automated alerting thresholds. Collect customer feedback and iterate.
